text:
sophia: quick sync – i'm putting a short PRD draft in the drive for "usage bands" (tiered soft limits + hard caps) and billing fallbacks. need buy-in on: per-tenant vs per-key defaults, UI affordances for customers, and how the API surfaces overage vs throttling. link: https://drive.redwood/usage-bands-draft :point_up:
liam: skimmed it. main question: are bands enforced server-side with 429 responses, or do we offer a soft-warning path that returns 200+warning header?
anita: from a design POV customers asked for a clear place in console where they can see current band, projected spend, and a single-click bump request. want to avoid modal sprawl. maybe an inline "request higher band" CTA next to limit numbers.
sophia: +1. proposal: default behavior = soft-band alarms (no request blocking) until band 3, after which requests get throttled (429). billing: soft-band usage billed normally; hard cap prevents further usage.
ryan: pricing semantics—if we keep soft-bands bill-as-you-go, we need a clear contract: "band increases don't retroactively change previous invoice rates". also need to define per-token rounding and embedding unit conversion.
liam: implementation note: we should expose an API header for clients so SDKs can show warnings: e.g.,
```
X-RateBand: 2
X-Band-Usage: 945000
X-Band-Cap: 1000000
```
and an error payload for hard cap: { "error": "band_cap_exceeded", "retry_after": 60 }
ryan: agree on headers. also require an event in billing that maps band changes to invoice metadata so accountants can reconcile spikes.
anita: small edge case: orgs with multiple keys — console must aggregate across keys and show per-key drilldown. dont show duplicate alerts.
sophia: good catch. decision item: default to per-tenant metering (aggregate) and allow per-key opt-in via policy config. anyone opposed?
liam: ok with that. follow-up: need to decide on burst behavior — allow short bursts above band for <5s or strictly enforce steady-state? I'd prefer brief bursts to avoid UX regressions on chatty apps.
sophia: leaning burst-allowed up to a small token budget that replenishes, with rate smoothing. we'll capture specifics in the PRD acceptance criteria.
ryan: billing edge-case: if a customer is in band 1 and requests an emergency bump that we manually approve mid-cycle, how do we prorate? propose prorate by days remaining in billing period and include a line item labeled "band upgrade (prorated)".
quota-bot: Reminder: there is an open RFC #214 on quota semantics that overlaps. Please reference before finalizing.
sophia: noted, i'll fold RFC #214 links and call out the overlap. action items: liam to draft API header spec + sample error payloads (ETA 48h), anita to mock console wire with per-tenant summary + per-key drilldown (ETA 72h), ryan to write billing proration appendix (ETA 72h). i'll consolidate into PRD v0.1 and circle back for signoff. :white_check_mark:
liam: will do. tagging @anita and @ryan for visibility. :+1:
anita: will add a small mobile layout note.
ryan: adding accounting example to appendix (export csv schema).
sophia: thanks all — i'll create the PRD doc now and schedule a 30m sync if anything blocks.
